# Historical NAT-T / UDP ownership auditors

`source-manifest.json` registers 38 literal source files (35 Python and3 Go,
275085 bytes) under `sources/`. Every file matches its original registered SHA256.
The manifest is copied unchanged from the external reviewed bundle; its SHA256
is `c206f729e4ead2430be02b297f86c833fa9820aad736598a8b9ccbe9ff0002e7`.
The directory attributes preserve the audited historical bytes, including line
endings. Do not format these archived source copies.

These sources implement original source extraction, exact whole-object
construction/verification, real capture-close accounting, complete native/CLI
and stats checks, and actual Windows console-cell checks. They retain explicit
historical paths, dependencies and source-specific producer requirements. Inspect
each original CLI before running it with `python -B -X utf8`; use a fresh external
destination and keep original captures, keys, frozen plans and closed execution
receipts. An edited/path-adapted source needs its own hash and producer receipt.
No old certificate authorizes relabeling a new execution.

No capture, key, complete plan/case/expected object, export, image, binary or log
is included. The manifest links those external artifacts by path and hash only.
The [counts and limitations](../../../../../../../../docs/exec-plans/shark-public-corpus-20261025/natt-udp-ownership-a82.md)
separate event/flow/EOF counts, actual producer commits, default Wireshark CoAP
differences, the corrected footer auditor and the still-open OSPFv3 work.
